1.mascotDialogue: All that splittin' is just bookkeepin' — the real sortin' work happens entirely in the merge step, comparin' two already-sorted halves and interleavin' 'em right.

2.mascotDialogue: Lines 9 and 10 are the merge's heart — compare the fronts of both halves, take the smaller, advance only that side. Lines 12 and 13 mop up whichever half's still got leftovers once the other one runs dry.

3.mascotDialogue: Notice this view don't show swaps a-tall — merge sort don't swap elements in place, it writes the smaller of two fronts into a fresh spot, every single comparison.

4.mascotDialogue: Easy to think the merge's 'done' the second the main comparison loop ends — but one side near always finishes 'fore the other, and forgettin' to drain them leftovers loses real data, quiet as can be.
